raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #62121. Apply sender-cache invalidations between multimodal renders so an engine cache-miss report cannot remove an entry between the processor's cache lookup and merge.

## Claims

- In-flight renders complete without the reported `Expected a cached item` assertion; already-queued renders consume pending invalidations before looking up cached data.
- Unrelated outputs keep flowing while multimodal processing or cache invalidation is blocked.
- Ignore uncached hashes and coalesce duplicate miss reports, avoiding unbounded notification growth on pre-rendered `features` traffic that never invokes the renderer.

## Validation

Current follow-up implementation (`d2097ba5`), macOS arm64 CPU, Python 3.13.15 / PyTorch 2.14.1:

- `pytest -p pytest_skipgc tests/multimodal/test_cache.py -k "not sleep" -q`: **29 passed, 1 deselected**. Includes LRU, SHM/IPC, the original forced-interleaving regression, coalescing/clear behavior, and a multi-hash failure with concurrent notifications.
- `pytest -p pytest_skipgc tests/renderers/test_warmup.py tests/renderers/test_executor_replace.py -q`: **28 passed**.
- The local `pytest_skipgc` plugin applies the repository's `skip_global_cleanup` marker to avoid the previously observed macOS torch teardown crash; it does not modify test assertions. SHM tests ran with local shared-memory access enabled.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, format, typos, mypy and Buildkite test tethering. `actionlint` was skipped; no workflow file changed. `git diff --check` passed.
- A method-level comparison using the real renderer/processor/LRU cache and the submitted `dc1a962` queue/drain methods reproduced the backlog: 1,000 absent hashes retained 1,000 records before and 0 after; 200 notifications for one cached hash retained 200 before and 1 after. The next render resent the payload in both cases. This was not a full baseline-tree pytest run.

The original assertion regression previously failed on pristine `a0e7137c` and passed on submitted commit `dc1a962`. That submitted implementation also has Linux CPU validation (27 passed, 1 deselected) and A800 serving evidence below. **The current coalescing follow-up has not been rerun on Linux or GPU; the historical serving measurements are not measurements of this follow-up.**

<details>
<summary>Historical A800 serving comparison for submitted commit dc1a962</summary>

Qwen2-VL-2B @ 895c3a49, A800 80GB PCIe, localhost HTTP using the reporter's pause/resume plus background-image load, no server-side hook. Five-minute trigger and two-minute control per arm:

| arm | rounds | target asserts | image requests | ok | other 500 | stream errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main trigger | 164 | 18 | 32,138 | 31,794 | 196 | 130 |
| dc1a962 trigger | 164 | 0 | 31,934 | 31,565 | 199 | 170 |
| main control | 56 | 0 | 24,632 | 24,632 | 0 | 0 |
| dc1a962 control | 56 | 0 | 25,070 | 25,070 | 0 | 0 |

Twelve fixed public-image responses were byte-identical for text, finish reason and completion-token count. Remaining errors were the existing P1-miss class; internal-error lines increased from 344 to 369 (1.07% to 1.16%). No overall error-rate improvement is claimed.

</details>

## Details

The output handler previously invalidated the sender cache on the asyncio thread while the renderer performed its lookup and merge on its single-worker multimodal executor.

The handler now records missed hashes before publishing the associated outputs. Only hashes currently present in the sender cache are retained. A short lock protects a pending set; each render swaps that set before its first lookup. Membership checks and cache invalidation execute outside the lock. Failed invalidation restores the current and remaining hashes without discarding newly arrived notifications. Cache clear retains its existing behavior; stale notifications become no-ops at the next render boundary.

This avoids a second executor job and queue/set mirrored state. Pending records can briefly outlive the cache entry they reference, so this does not claim that their count always equals the instantaneous live cache size. Sync LLM retains direct invalidation.

This is distinct from #34749's assertion-to-error conversion and #61656's endpoint retries. P1 drift itself, automatic HTTP retries, and #62123's SHM handle issue are out of scope. The issue came from a public report and was investigated with constructed reproductions; it was not encountered in the submitter's production workload. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation and validation, including this follow-up review.

---

<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** The change stays within renderer cache invalidation and output handling; no scheduler or model-runner changes.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** CPU regression coverage and historical serving evidence are distinguished above; tests remain in the existing Buildkite-wired suite.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Concise comments, a shared renderer fixture, and changed-file checks.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, evidence, remaining error class and validation limits are explicit.

</details>

nodes.body: Could you run `vllm bench mm-processor` to ensure there are no performance regressions?

Ran `vllm bench mm-processor` comparing the PR base `a0e7137c` with current head `d2097ba5` on an A800 80GB, Qwen2-VL-2B @ `895c3a49`, BF16/TP=1/eager. The initial experiment uses three fresh processes per revision/cache setting, alternating order, 256 synthetic prompts after 16 warmups. All 3,072 measured requests completed.

Below are means across the three runs, with their min/max. The P95/P99 rows are averages of per-run quantiles.

| Cache | Metric | Base mean [min, max] | Patch mean [min, max] | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 GiB | Batch wall time (s) | 5.3228 [5.3169, 5.3301] | 5.3362 [5.3292, 5.3462] | +0.25% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing mean (ms) | 2.7862 [2.6805, 2.8712] | 2.8160 [2.7919, 2.8339] | +1.07% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing P95 (ms) | 4.3179 [4.0639, 4.5351] | 4.3649 [4.3162, 4.4063] | +1.09% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing P99 (ms) | 4.4947 [4.2661, 4.7086] | 4.7631 [4.4970, 5.2637] | +5.97% |
| 0 GiB | Batch wall time (s) | 5.3268 [5.3096, 5.3414] | 5.3314 [5.3216, 5.3379] | +0.09% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing mean (ms) | 2.4980 [2.4281, 2.5433] | 2.5266 [2.4928, 2.5716] | +1.15% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing P95 (ms) | 3.8566 [3.7235, 3.9292] | 3.8966 [3.8504, 3.9720] | +1.04% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing P99 (ms) | 3.9404 [3.8573, 4.0005] | 4.4177 [3.9112, 5.1061] | +12.11% |

The mean batch-time changes are small (+0.25% with caching, +0.09% without), but the initial preprocessing P99s were higher. I therefore ran a separate 1,024-prompt/32-warmup pair per cache setting; all 4,096 requests completed:

| Cache | Metric | Base | Patch | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 GiB | Batch wall time (s) | 20.5814 | 20.6302 | +0.24% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing mean (ms) | 2.8296 | 2.7502 | -2.81% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing P95 (ms) | 4.5388 | 4.4108 | -2.82% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing P99 (ms) | 4.8359 | 4.5907 | -5.07% |
| 0 GiB | Batch wall time (s) | 20.4615 | 20.5256 | +0.31% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing mean (ms) | 2.5320 | 2.4987 | -1.32% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing P95 (ms) | 4.1531 | 4.0509 | -2.46% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing P99 (ms) | 4.6277 | 4.2601 | -7.94% |

The larger-sample pairs did not reproduce the initial P99 increase. Tail results remain variable; these measurements show small observed mean-time differences in this tested configuration.

Since the internal stage timer excludes the added drain, I also timed complete real `render_cmpl` calls over three repetitions: mean changes were -0.24% for cache hits, +0.55% for unique misses and +0.58% with caching disabled. Those measurements include the new empty-drain/lock. These are offline/synchronous measurements; they do not exercise AsyncLLM's output loop, actual miss notifications, or contention.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and environment</summary>

Linux, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, NVIDIA driver 580.105.08. Both exact Python source revisions use the same official `7b6310c1` precompiled artifacts; that wheel commit differs from the base only in two AMD DeepSeek model files. The pinned model files and changed-source hashes were checked.

For batch wall time, both benchmark copies identically export the existing `total_time` variable as an additional JSON field; the measured processing is unchanged. The source PR was not changed.

```bash
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_PLUGINS=""
# MODEL is a local snapshot of Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct at
# 895c3a49bc3fa70a340399125c650a463535e71c.
# Run CACHE_GB=4 and 0; three fresh processes per revision/configuration.
vllm bench mm-processor \
  --model "$MODEL" --dataset-name random-mm \
  --num-prompts 256 --num-warmups 16 --seed 42 \
  --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config '{(224,224,1):0.5,(672,672,1):0.5}' \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
  --mm-processor-cache-type lru --mm-processor-cache-gb "$CACHE_GB" \
  --metric-percentiles 50,95,99 --disable-tqdm --output-json "$RESULT"
```
The separate follow-up changes only `--num-prompts 1024 --num-warmups 32`.

</details>

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

**Nothing blocking.** The comments below are optional suggestions. There is no need to push a fix for them before merging.

<!-- bhrv:fed34a39e05e4b19 -->

🟡 (optional) Servers that only receive pre-rendered `features` requests will keep growing a miss-hash backlog in memory that is never freed. On the base branch these misses cost nothing. `queue_mm_cache_invalidations` appends every reported miss hash to `_pending_mm_cache_invalidations`. Only `_process_multimodal` drains it, and the `/generate` features path never calls that method. Fix: bound the backlog by distinct live entries. Skip hashes the sender cache does not hold (`is_cached_item`), and dedupe pending hashes so the queue never outgrows the cache. Hashes an in-flight render repopulates have already resent data, so dropping them is safe.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is a token-in-token-out `/generate` server whose multimodal traffic arrives as `features` with `kwargs_data` items set to None. The `features` branch in serving.py builds `mm_input` directly. That branch never calls `render_cmpl_async` or `_process_multimodal`. When P1 lacks the hash, `get_and_update_features` raises `MultiModalCacheMissError` (cache/base.py:478). The output handler at async_llm.py:882-891 queues every such hash whenever `renderer.mm_processor_cache` is not None, which holds with the default LRU sender cache. The only reader is `_drain_mm_cache_invalidations`, called at base.py:926 from `_process_multimodal`. So on such a server the `SimpleQueue` grows by one string per missed item per failed request and is never freed. The base branch called `invalidate` (a `dict.pop` in lru.py:80) right away and kept nothing.

**Verification:** `queue_mm_cache_invalidations` (base.py ~396-400) puts every reported hash on `_pending_mm_cache_invalidations`. The only drain is at the top of `_process_multimodal` (base.py ~926), which the `features` branch (serving.py 269-290) never calls. On the base branch the handler called `mm_processor_cache.invalidate(mm_hash)` right away, so nothing was kept.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:nit -->

nodes.body:
**Nothing blocking.** The comments below are optional suggestions. There is no need to push a fix for them before merging.

<!-- bhrv:4fe4055e007621ac -->

🟣 pre-existing, not blocking: pre-existing: Online pooling and embedding requests with images can still hit `Expected a cached item` after this fix. Their sync renders run on the multi-worker `_executor`, not the single-worker `_mm_executor`. The drain at base.py:932 then runs on a pool thread. It can pop a hash while an async render on `_mm_executor`, or another pool render, is between lookup and merge. Fix: make sure no other render can be between lookup and merge when pending invalidations are applied. One way is to send every online `_process_multimodal` call through `_mm_executor`. Another is to hold one lock across the drain plus `mm_processor.apply`.
_A small fix can ride a push you are already making; otherwise a short reply is enough._

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Online pooling serving calls `io_processor.render_async`. That is `make_async(self.render, executor=self.renderer._executor)` (pooling/base/io_processor.py:71-72), and `renderer._executor` is a `_SwappableExecutor(max_workers=renderer_num_workers)` (renderers/base.py:144). `render` calls sync `render_cmpl`/`render_chat` (io_processor.py:260-275), which goes through `_process_tokens` and calls `_process_multimodal` directly (base.py:978). So `_drain_mm_cache_invalidations` (base.py:932) runs on a pool thread, concurrently with renders on `_mm_executor`. A queued miss hash is popped from the LRU (`invalidate` is `self._cache.pop`, lru.py:83) in the middle of the other render. That render's later `get_and_update_item` then fails `assert mm_item is not None, f"Expected a cached item for {mm_hash=}"` (lru.py:60). The base branch had the same race, with invalidation on the event-loop thread, so this is not a regression. The PR's claim that renders cannot lose an entry between lookup and merge does not hold for this path, because the drain only serializes with work on `_mm_executor`.

**Verification:** A `/tokenize` request with an image runs on `_mm_executor`, and its drain at base.py:932 calls `self.mm_processor_cache.invalidate(...)` while a pooling render on the `_executor` thread is between lookup and merge. That pooling render can then still hit `Expected a cached item`. On the base branch, async_llm.py called `mm_processor_cache.invalidate` directly and already raced the same way.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:pre_existing -->

🟡 (optional) Servers that only receive pre-rendered `features` requests will keep growing a miss-hash backlog in memory that is never freed. On the base branch these misses cost nothing. `queue_mm_cache_invalidations` appends every reported miss hash to `_pending_mm_cache_invalidations`. Only `_process_multimodal` drains it, and the `/generate` features path never calls that method. Fix: bound the backlog by distinct live entries. Skip hashes the sender cache does not hold (`is_cached_item`), and dedupe pending hashes so the queue never outgrows the cache. Hashes an in-flight render repopulates have already resent data, so dropping them is safe.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is a token-in-token-out `/generate` server whose multimodal traffic arrives as `features` with `kwargs_data` items set to None. The `features` branch in serving.py builds `mm_input` directly. That branch never calls `render_cmpl_async` or `_process_multimodal`. When P1 lacks the hash, `get_and_update_features` raises `MultiModalCacheMissError` (cache/base.py:478). The output handler at async_llm.py:882-891 queues every such hash whenever `renderer.mm_processor_cache` is not None, which holds with the default LRU sender cache. The only reader is `_drain_mm_cache_invalidations`, called at base.py:926 from `_process_multimodal`. So on such a server the `SimpleQueue` grows by one string per missed item per failed request and is never freed. The base branch called `invalidate` (a `dict.pop` in lru.py:80) right away and kept nothing.

**Verification:** `queue_mm_cache_invalidations` (base.py ~396-400) puts every reported hash on `_pending_mm_cache_invalidations`. The only drain is at the top of `_process_multimodal` (base.py ~926), which the `features` branch (serving.py 269-290) never calls. On the base branch the handler called `mm_processor_cache.invalidate(mm_hash)` right away, so nothing was kept.

</details>

🟣 pre-existing, not blocking: pre-existing: Online pooling and embedding requests with images can still hit `Expected a cached item` after this fix. Their sync renders run on the multi-worker `_executor`, not the single-worker `_mm_executor`. The drain at base.py:932 then runs on a pool thread. It can pop a hash while an async render on `_mm_executor`, or another pool render, is between lookup and merge. Fix: make sure no other render can be between lookup and merge when pending invalidations are applied. One way is to send every online `_process_multimodal` call through `_mm_executor`. Another is to hold one lock across the drain plus `mm_processor.apply`.
_A small fix can ride a push you are already making; otherwise a short reply is enough._

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Online pooling serving calls `io_processor.render_async`. That is `make_async(self.render, executor=self.renderer._executor)` (pooling/base/io_processor.py:71-72), and `renderer._executor` is a `_SwappableExecutor(max_workers=renderer_num_workers)` (renderers/base.py:144). `render` calls sync `render_cmpl`/`render_chat` (io_processor.py:260-275), which goes through `_process_tokens` and calls `_process_multimodal` directly (base.py:978). So `_drain_mm_cache_invalidations` (base.py:932) runs on a pool thread, concurrently with renders on `_mm_executor`. A queued miss hash is popped from the LRU (`invalidate` is `self._cache.pop`, lru.py:83) in the middle of the other render. That render's later `get_and_update_item` then fails `assert mm_item is not None, f"Expected a cached item for {mm_hash=}"` (lru.py:60). The base branch had the same race, with invalidation on the event-loop thread, so this is not a regression. The PR's claim that renders cannot lose an entry between lookup and merge does not hold for this path, because the drain only serializes with work on `_mm_executor`.

**Verification:** A `/tokenize` request with an image runs on `_mm_executor`, and its drain at base.py:932 calls `self.mm_processor_cache.invalidate(...)` while a pooling render on the `_executor` thread is between lookup and merge. That pooling render can then still hit `Expected a cached item`. On the base branch, async_llm.py called `mm_processor_cache.invalidate` directly and already raced the same way.

</details>

issue_comments.body: Could you run `vllm bench mm-processor` to ensure there are no performance regressions?

Ran `vllm bench mm-processor` comparing the PR base `a0e7137c` with current head `d2097ba5` on an A800 80GB, Qwen2-VL-2B @ `895c3a49`, BF16/TP=1/eager. The initial experiment uses three fresh processes per revision/cache setting, alternating order, 256 synthetic prompts after 16 warmups. All 3,072 measured requests completed.

Below are means across the three runs, with their min/max. The P95/P99 rows are averages of per-run quantiles.

| Cache | Metric | Base mean [min, max] | Patch mean [min, max] | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 GiB | Batch wall time (s) | 5.3228 [5.3169, 5.3301] | 5.3362 [5.3292, 5.3462] | +0.25% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing mean (ms) | 2.7862 [2.6805, 2.8712] | 2.8160 [2.7919, 2.8339] | +1.07% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing P95 (ms) | 4.3179 [4.0639, 4.5351] | 4.3649 [4.3162, 4.4063] | +1.09% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing P99 (ms) | 4.4947 [4.2661, 4.7086] | 4.7631 [4.4970, 5.2637] | +5.97% |
| 0 GiB | Batch wall time (s) | 5.3268 [5.3096, 5.3414] | 5.3314 [5.3216, 5.3379] | +0.09% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing mean (ms) | 2.4980 [2.4281, 2.5433] | 2.5266 [2.4928, 2.5716] | +1.15% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing P95 (ms) | 3.8566 [3.7235, 3.9292] | 3.8966 [3.8504, 3.9720] | +1.04% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing P99 (ms) | 3.9404 [3.8573, 4.0005] | 4.4177 [3.9112, 5.1061] | +12.11% |

The mean batch-time changes are small (+0.25% with caching, +0.09% without), but the initial preprocessing P99s were higher. I therefore ran a separate 1,024-prompt/32-warmup pair per cache setting; all 4,096 requests completed:

| Cache | Metric | Base | Patch | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 GiB | Batch wall time (s) | 20.5814 | 20.6302 | +0.24% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing mean (ms) | 2.8296 | 2.7502 | -2.81% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing P95 (ms) | 4.5388 | 4.4108 | -2.82% |
| 4 GiB | Preprocessing P99 (ms) | 4.8359 | 4.5907 | -5.07% |
| 0 GiB | Batch wall time (s) | 20.4615 | 20.5256 | +0.31% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing mean (ms) | 2.5320 | 2.4987 | -1.32% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing P95 (ms) | 4.1531 | 4.0509 | -2.46% |
| 0 GiB | Preprocessing P99 (ms) | 4.6277 | 4.2601 | -7.94% |

The larger-sample pairs did not reproduce the initial P99 increase. Tail results remain variable; these measurements show small observed mean-time differences in this tested configuration.

Since the internal stage timer excludes the added drain, I also timed complete real `render_cmpl` calls over three repetitions: mean changes were -0.24% for cache hits, +0.55% for unique misses and +0.58% with caching disabled. Those measurements include the new empty-drain/lock. These are offline/synchronous measurements; they do not exercise AsyncLLM's output loop, actual miss notifications, or contention.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and environment</summary>

Linux, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, NVIDIA driver 580.105.08. Both exact Python source revisions use the same official `7b6310c1` precompiled artifacts; that wheel commit differs from the base only in two AMD DeepSeek model files. The pinned model files and changed-source hashes were checked.

For batch wall time, both benchmark copies identically export the existing `total_time` variable as an additional JSON field; the measured processing is unchanged. The source PR was not changed.
